full_judgment: a. Principle that legal burden of proof always remains on the prosecution is the most fundamental principle of our Criminal Jurisprudence and is much older than the Evidence Act, because it was the principle of common law administered by Apex Court of the Sub-Continent. It is, thus, elementary principle of criminal law that in all criminal cases the burden of proof lies upon the prosecution to bring the guilt home to the door of accused persons beyond any reasonable doubt. Proof beyond reasonable doubt means proof of an offence with the certainty of criminal law; the certainty is that offence is committed and that no other person but the accused person on the evidence committed offence. It is, also, to be borne in mind that vague hunches cannot take the place of Judicial evaluation. Presumption, conjectures and surmises cannot take the field of evidence. The conviction on the basis of shaky and unreliable evidence by witnesses would not be at all proper and legal.
